elements.element: Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its affiliates
elements.evidence: IBM will defend and indemnify Customer and its Enterprise against any third-party claim

elements.element: Trigger: third-party claim alleging Services or Deliverables infringe IP
elements.evidence: (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe any intellectual property right

elements.element: Trigger: data breach caused by Vendor
elements.evidence: (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer data caused by IBM

elements.element: Trigger: Vendor gross negligence / wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: (d) IBM's gross negligence or willful misconduct
a. promptly notifies IBM in writing of the claim

elements.element: Procedure: Vendor control of defence and settlement
elements.evidence: allows IBM to control ... the defense and any related settlement negotiations
cooperates with IBM in, the defense and any related settlement negotiations

elements.element: Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content
elements.evidence: related, directly or indirectly, to the Content

elements.element: Customer indemnity limited to Customer's breach of law
elements.evidence: or Customer's breach of applicable law
IBM will indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Customer ... infringe that party's patent, trademark, copyright, or trade secret
exclusion list covers only items provided by Customer, Customer modification, and Services Recipient claims; no combination carve-out
no reference to Customer specifications anywhere in the exclusions

elements.element: Fallback remedies: procure/continue use, modify, replace
elements.evidence: enable Customer to continue to use the Materials or Base Components, or to modify them, or replace them with non-infringing
IBM will give Customer a credit equal to the amount Customer paid IBM

elements.element: Fallback: super-cap of 3× annual fees on Vendor indemnity
elements.evidence: credit capped at 'a maximum of twelve (12) months of applicable charges'; no 3× annual fees super-cap

reasons: All preferred atomic elements are satisfied: the inserted Section 8.3 supplies Vendor defence and indemnity for Customer and its Enterprise across IP infringement in the Services/Deliverables, IBM's breach of law, IBM-caused data breach, and IBM's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, and the existing notice/control/cooperation mechanics remain.

The replacement of exclusion item 3 narrows the Customer-side trigger from any Services Recipient claim related to the Services to the Content and Customer's breach of applicable law, matching the preferred limitation.
Edits are surgical (one concise insertion plus one short trigger swap); no hold-harmless language, extra indemnitees, Customer defence duty, or fallback-only remedies or super-cap were imported.

Intent risk: the untouched sole-remedy sentence 'This is IBM's entire obligation to Customer with regard to any claim of infringement' now sits in tension with new Section 8.3(a), which could be read to neutralise the added IP indemnity; a 'except as provided in Section 8.3' carve-out would remove the contradiction.

Intent risk: 'the Content' is used as a capitalised term in the revised item 3 but is not shown as defined in the resolved definitions, creating a possible undefined-term reference (preferred wording would be 'Customer-provided content').
Fallback bargain is independently incomplete (no combination or specification exclusions, no 3× annual fees super-cap), but that is immaterial because the locked target level (preferred) is met.
